title: UC Berkeley Researchers Examine Monopsony Power in Labor Market
discussion_signal: The post explicitly identifies the NBER working paper Monopsony Makes it Big and frames labor-market power as arising from several interacting mechanisms: search frictions, worker preferences, and employer concentration. It connects the framework to antitrust and labor policy without collapsing observed wage markdowns into a single measure of employer power.
linked_research_question: How should U.S. researchers and policymakers distinguish employer concentration, search frictions, worker preferences, and wage-setting practices when measuring labor-market power and designing remedies?
limits: The post is a concise institutional translation and does not provide a single U.S. industry estimate
It does not establish worker welfare effects or rank firms by monopsony power
A single LinkedIn post is not representative of workers, firms, or policymakers
